title: Testing punctual purity on mixed-characteristic complete traits
statement:
For a prime $\ell$ and $A=\mathbf F_\ell$, use ordinary small-etale derived categories and Tate twists [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist]. If $W$ is a regular Noetherian scheme with $\ell$ invertible [def-weil-regular-scheme], say that $W$ is punctually pure at $w\in W$ when, for $W_w=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{W,w}$, $d_w=\dim\mathcal O_{W,w}$ and its closed-point inclusion $j_w:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(w)\hookrightarrow W_w$, the Kummer fundamental-class map
$$A_{\kappa(w)}\longrightarrow j_w^!A_{W_w}(d_w)[2d_w]$$
of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus] is an isomorphism. Say that $W$ is punctually pure when this holds at every point. Local rings and residue fields are as in [def-weil-residue-field], affine spectra as in [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and dimension as in [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

A trait here is $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ for a discrete valuation ring: a Noetherian local domain of dimension one whose maximal ideal is principal. A complete strictly henselian trait has $R$ complete for its maximal-ideal topology and henselian with separably closed residue field (henselian means that every simple root over the residue field of a monic polynomial over $R$ lifts to a root over $R$). Mixed characteristic means that $\operatorname{Frac}R$ has characteristic zero and the residue field has positive characteristic.

Fix $\ell$. Suppose that every integral regular scheme $V$, flat and quasi-projective of finite type over a complete strictly henselian mixed-characteristic trait $S$ on which $\ell$ is invertible, is punctually pure. Then every regular Noetherian scheme $W$ on which $\ell$ is invertible is punctually pure. Here flat and finite type have the meanings of [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and quasi-projective means that $V$ admits a locally closed immersion into $\mathbf P^N_S$ for some finite $N$. No excellence hypothesis is made on $W$.

source.place: Expose XVI, section 3.7 first paragraph, printed p.254 (Fujiwara 2002 Corollary 6.1.5 reduction), with Proposition 3.2.4 (completion invariance) and Proposition 3.2.5 (prime-field/equal-characteristic case), printed pp.244--245. Complete-trait formulation obtained by first completing the strictly henselian regular local test ring.

proof.text: Fix $w\in W$ and put $R=\mathcal O_{W,w}$. This is regular local by [def-weil-regular-scheme]. By [lem-per-trait-test-strict-completion-input], it is enough to prove the closed-point Kummer map for $B=\widehat{R^{\mathrm{sh}}}$ is an isomorphism. That input supplies regularity, Noetherianity, completeness, strict henselianity, unchanged dimension, separably closed residue field and invertibility of $\ell$. By [lem-sc-regular-local-domain], $B$ is a domain. If $B$ has positive characteristic it contains its prime field $\mathbf F_p$. If its residue characteristic is zero then every nonzero integer is a unit, so it contains $\mathbf Q$. In both cases [lem-per-trait-test-prime-field-local-input] proves its closed-point map is an isomorphism. It remains to handle mixed characteristic $(0,p)$ with $p\ne\ell$.

source.place: Expose XVI Definitions 3.2.1--3.2.2, Propositions 3.2.4--3.2.5, pp.244--245; section 3.7 first paragraph, p.254. Fresh one-level assembly by Q08 after the exclusion return; simultaneous approximation and derived supported continuity are separate unsplit inputs.

proof.text: Put $d=\dim B$. In mixed characteristic $d\ge1$: a dimension-zero regular local ring has zero maximal ideal and is a field, so cannot have different ring and residue characteristics. Choose $d$ generators of the maximal ideal by [def-weil-regular-scheme]; [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence] makes them a regular sequence. Apply [lem-per-trait-test-mixed-regular-pair-models] to these parameters. It provides $Z_a\hookrightarrow V_a$ over a complete strictly henselian mixed-characteristic trait $S$, with $V_a$ integral regular affine, flat, finite type and quasi-projective over $S$, regular characteristic-$p$ quotients $Z_a$, compatible regular equations of length $d$, and limiting pair $\operatorname{Spec}k\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}B$.

source.place: Expose XVI Definitions 3.2.1--3.2.2, Propositions 3.2.4--3.2.5, pp.244--245; section 3.7 first paragraph, p.254. Fresh one-level assembly by Q08 after the exclusion return; simultaneous approximation and derived supported continuity are separate unsplit inputs.

proof.text: The assumed trait test applies to every $V_a$ supplied in Step 2, so $V_a$ is punctually pure. Each $V_a$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]; the approximation also states Noetherianity for $Z_a$. At every $z\in Z_a$, its local ring is regular and is an $\mathbf F_p$-algebra with $\ell$ invertible. Apply [lem-per-trait-test-prime-field-local-input] at that local ring. Thus $Z_a$ is punctually pure by [def-per-punctual-purity]. The compatible length-$d$ equations give constant codimension $d$ by [def-per-regular-closed-immersion-codimension], exactly as stated by the approximation. Conditions (b) and (c) of [lem-per-punctual-purity-two-of-three] therefore imply (a): the canonical map $A_{Z_a}\to i_a^!A_{V_a}(d)[2d]$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Expose XVI Definitions 3.2.1--3.2.2, Propositions 3.2.4--3.2.5, pp.244--245; section 3.7 first paragraph, p.254. Fresh one-level assembly by Q08 after the exclusion return; simultaneous approximation and derived supported continuity are separate unsplit inputs.

proof.text: By the adjunction [def-per-closed-support-plus-adjunction] and derived supported-Hom formula [lem-amb-closed-support-hom], derived global sections of the Step 3 map identify with $\gamma_a:R\Gamma(Z_a,A)\to R\Gamma_{Z_a}(V_a,A(d))[2d]$. Each $\gamma_a$ is an isomorphism. Apply [lem-per-trait-test-supported-kummer-continuity] with $c=d$: all stages and limits are affine regular Noetherian, the indexing set is small directed, $\ell$ is invertible, and the regular equations are preserved by Step 2. Its derived comparison square identifies the colimit arrow with the specified limiting Kummer arrow $\gamma$, hence $\gamma$ is an isomorphism. For the separably closed residue field $k$, [lem-exc-etale-sheaves-gsets-point] identifies its small etale topos with sets (the Galois group is trivial). Module objects are consequently ordinary $A$-modules and sections are exact and conservative. The same adjunction and supported-Hom formula therefore identify $\gamma$ with derived sections of $A_k\to j_B^!A_B(d)[2d]$, and sections detect its isomorphism: its cohomology maps are detected by this exact equivalence, and [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology] then applies.

proof.text: The descent implication of Step 1 proves the canonical closed-point map for $R$ is an isomorphism. Since $w$ was arbitrary, [def-per-punctual-purity] gives punctual purity of $W$. The empty scheme satisfies this pointwise statement vacuously.
